subject: Action required: narrow runtime data-use clause for Greenline pilot
messages:
From: Sarah Harris <sarah.harris@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@greenlinehealth.com
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline: runtime data use & subprocessors — pilot constraints

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. We're excited to move forward with the pilot, but Legal/Procurement flagged a few items in the attached redline (Greenline_DPA_Redline_v2.pdf) that we need explicit confirmation on before procurement can sign. High level:

- We need an explicit statement that Redwood will not use Greenline runtime data to train models (including internal model improvement pipelines) unless we opt-in in writing.
- Clarification of telemetry/telemetry retention: the redline requests a 30-day max for any inference logs that include customer inputs; your default policy in the doc seems longer.
- A request to include a runtime subprocessor disclosure: list of subprocessors that may handle runtime logs and KV cache (or a process for notifying us).

Can you loop in Product and Security so we can get technical confirmation and proposed contractual language? Procurement wants a response by EOD Tuesday (May 18). I've attached the redline and a short suggested wording in the cover notes.

Thanks —
Sarah
Sarah Harris
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
Greenline Health

Attachments: Greenline_DPA_Redline_v2.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: DPA redline: runtime data use & subprocessors — pilot constraints

Sarah — thank you for the redline and the clear asks. Looping in Olga (Legal) and Irene (Product) to confirm technical constraints and to propose contractual language that balances Greenline's request and our operational needs. Marissa is on for any commercial impacts on the pilot SOW.

Quick ask for Product/Security: can you confirm the following by EOD Tuesday so Procurement can proceed?

1) We can commit to a "no-training" clause for the pilot (no training of models using customer-provided inference inputs) if Security can attest that logs used for telemetry are separated and have a 30-day retention cap or are pseudonymized.

2) We need a clear subprocessors disclosure or a notification process for any runtime vendor that could access runtime logs/KV cache. Is a monthly notification + updated subprocessor list acceptable?

3) If runtime caching (KV cache) is required for latency, can we provide operational controls (auto-evict policy, retention limit, and encryption at rest) and surfacing in the Console (per-route toggle) to satisfy the ask?

Attaching the customer's redline for reference. Olga — if you can draft two short contract options (tight language and fallback language) that would be ideal.

Thanks —
Vivek
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Vivek / Sarah — I reviewed the redline and the asks. High level legal position and options:

Option A (preferred by customer): Explicit "no training" clause + 30-day retention for inference logs that contain customer inputs. Require customer opt-in for any use beyond that.

Risks: Option A will require us to put operational guardrails in place and to be explicit about the subprocessor notification timeline (monthly updates may be acceptable, but security needs to vet which vendors we include on the list for runtime processing). This will also affect our standard telemetry retention for a segment of the account.

Option B (fallback): Allow broader telemetry for product improvement but agree to pseudonymization and aggregated telemetry only, plus a formal SLA to notify and get consent before using inputs to train models. Retention can be set to 90 days for aggregated telemetry and 30 days for raw inference logs.

Irene — can you confirm whether we can implement Option A operationally for the pilot (30-day raw log retention, per-account opt-in flag for training, subprocessor disclosure process)? If not, draft the technical language for Option B so I can propose that to Greenline.

Sarah — I attached a short proposed wording (proposed-runtime-clause-draft.txt). If Greenline can accept Option B with the pseudonymization guarantees and a notification/consent path, procurement may be able to move faster.

Olga
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-runtime-clause-draft.txt

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Sarah Harris <sarah.harris@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline: runtime data use & subprocessors — pilot constraints

Olga / Vivek / Sarah — technical confirmation and proposed compromise below. TL;DR: we can meet the customer's core asks for the pilot with small operational work and a clear contract clause.

What we can deliver for pilot (concrete):
- No-training guarantee: we will add an explicit contract clause that we will not use Greenline inference inputs to train models during the pilot unless Greenline provides written consent. This maps to a per-account opt-in flag and a process to approve training use.
- Retention: implement 30-day retention for any raw inference logs that include customer inputs. After 30 days raw logs are auto-evicted. Aggregated telemetry (metrics, error rates) can be kept longer but will be pseudonymized.
- KV cache: we cannot fully disable KV caching without impacting latency for certain multimodal flows. We propose a per-route TTL (default 1 hour for sensitive routes) and an admin toggle in the Console to disable KV caching for the Greenline account. Encrypted at rest and access controls applied.
- Subprocessor disclosure: we can provide a current list of runtime subprocessors and commit to monthly updates; for any new subprocessor that would materially access raw inputs we will notify Greenline at least 30 days in advance.

Operational work: engineering will need a small config flag + retention enforcement for the account and a Console UI change to expose the toggle. Estimate: 3-4 engineering days of effort (can be scoped as high priority for the pilot).

Proposed next steps:
1) Olga: draft Option A contract language based on the attached text (I reviewed).
2) Vivek / Marissa: confirm commercial impact (pilot SOW timeline and any change in fees if we add retention features).
3) Sarah: if Greenline accepts the operational compromise, we ask for a signed SOW by May 25 so engineering can start.

I will update the Confluence doc with the exact retention behavior and link it in the proposed clause.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Product Lead, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
